title: Strict quotient tower and open tensor comparison interfaces
statement: For the completed coefficient categories, unbounded cochain complexes and strict positive quotient towers on schemes [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], define the strict open quotient tensor interfaces formerly declared in OpenTensorQuotientAugmentation. Towers and transpose retain every transition; Balanced retains its coefficient formula; Augmentation its homogeneous scalar-unit formula; ScalarCompatibility and ScalarComparison their actual coefficient-level normalizations. StrictSquare records balanced comparisons, finite coefficient-linear comparisons, their reduction equations, strict augmentation square and localized equality. RoosNormalization pins the augmentation to the first normalized tensor-completion coordinate. FiniteGeometry, FiniteExtensionModel, RestrictionPartitions and IntegralGeometry state the exact geometric properties. Comparison packages these with compatible ordinary and complete open comparisons. These are definitions or structures, with no existence assertion [def-sf-integral-open-operations, def-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison-data, def-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model-data, def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison]. ScalarComponents names exactly the original degreewise ScalarComparison.components proposition, without altering its meaning. In ScalarCompatibility, sections explicitly requires finite scalar restriction to carry every finite extension-by-zero summand to the identical completed-scalar extension summand. This normalization is necessary: unnormalized finite isomorphisms permit a sign twist, which does not preserve scalar-adjunction units. ScalarCompatibility retains only finite and sections; the unused systems and evaluation fields are pruned. ScalarComparison.iso and components retain the full strict quotient-tower comparison and all finite component equations.

statement_change.what: Prune the unused independent system comparison and its evaluation field. The old universal evaluation theorem is false: finite and systems are independently chosen isomorphisms, so negating just one gives another permitted choice but reverses its component on a nonzero module (identity open over a point, l=3). The actual scalar-unit and tensor-square proofs use only finite generator-normalized comparisons and ScalarComparison.iso, which already preserves all quotient transitions. Construct the finite normalized comparison directly from the proved generic open/scalar comparison; remove the false unused obligation instead of weakening it or assuming normalization.

previous.what: Repair the missing identity-on-extension-summands normalization of ScalarCompatibility. Without it, replacing both finite and systems by their negatives (and r by its negative) preserves every recorded field but reverses the asserted unit composite; for the identity open over a point with residue characteristic 3 and a nonzero degree-zero module the unit is not its negative. The new sections field records precisely the canonical identity formula promised by the source and the existing existence theorem; it does not assume any tower-unit equation.
